question: Which institute has developed an indigenously made point-of-care test kit for early diagnosis of Haemophilia A and Von Willebrand Disease?

options.text: All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS)

solution:
The correct answer is __**National Institute of Immunohaematology**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **ICMR-National Institute of Immunohaematology (NIIH)**, located in **Mumbai**, has developed an indigenously made **point-of-care (POC) test kit** for the early diagnosis of **Haemophilia A** and **Von Willebrand Disease (VWD)**.
 
• This development is a significant milestone in India's healthcare sector, as it addresses the challenge of diagnosing these **bleeding disorders** in resource-limited settings where sophisticated laboratory facilities are unavailable.
 
• The kit is designed to be **cost-effective** and **portable**, allowing for rapid testing at the bedside or in small clinics, which is crucial for timely clinical management.
 
• Traditionally, diagnosing these conditions requires expensive and time-consuming tests like **Factor VIII assays** or **VWF antigen tests**, which are often restricted to tertiary care hospitals in **major cities**.
